column1: #  - package specs, bodies, renamings and instantiations are packages; a child unit is named by its dotted name (Shapes.Extra); a generic package is the package it wraps;

#  - procedures and functions are functions: specifications, bodies (a specification and its body are both listed), expression functions, generic subprograms (at the line of the specification, not of the `generic` keyword), renamings, instantiations and nested subprograms; an operator function is named with its quotes;
#  - the operations declared in a protected type and the subprograms of a protected body are methods, and so is an entry;

#  - records, record extensions, enumerations, task types, protected types and single task or protected objects are classes; interface types are interfaces; every other type and every subtype is a type alias; the `is private` view of a type is not a definition, its full declaration is;
#  - record and protected components are fields;
#  - at package level, a number declaration or an object declared constant is a constant, any other object a variable; objects local to a subprogram are not definitions;
#  - not definitions: calls, parameters, generic formals, accept statements, task and protected bodies, `type T;`.
